runs.answer: As of the latest NHC public advisory, Hurricane Simon is a Category 2 hurricane on Mexico's Pacific coast. The newest is Intermediate Public Advisory Number 21A, issued 11:00 AM MST (1800 UTC) Monday Oct 12, 2026. Simon's center is near 20.2°N 106.6°W — about 60 mi (95 km) WSW of Cabo Corrientes and about 210 mi (335 km) S of Mazatlán — with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (165 km/h), minimum central pressure 965 mb, and it is drifting west at 2 mph (4 km/h). Watches/warnings in effect for Mexico: a Hurricane Warning for Las Islas Marías; a Hurricane Watch north of Cabo Corrientes to Bahia Tempehuaya; and a Tropical Storm Warning from Playa Perula to Cabo Corrientes. (The prior full advisory, Number 21 at 8:00 AM MST/1500 UTC, had Simon at 110 mph moving NW at 3 mph, and noted Mexico had downgraded the northern hurricane warning to a watch and to a tropical storm warning near Cabo Corrientes. NHC expects Simon to remain a hurricane through midweek and approach/come inland over west-central Mexico Wednesday-Thursday, with life-threatening flooding rain.)

runs.title: French supermarket cyberattack: what actually happened
runs.prompt: Today, Monday 12 October 2026, French supermarket chains have reported a cyber-attack that forced refrigerator systems to shut down and spoiled stock. A shopper would ask: which chains are affected, what exactly happened, and are stores still open? Using only plain page fetches, find out which supermarket chains were hit, what the attackers did, and what the companies have said. Start with BleepingComputer's report and the Guardian's report: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cyberattack-shuts-down-refrigerators-at-french-supermarkets/ and https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/12/cyber-attack-defrosts-refrigerators-france-supermarket-chains-intermarche-cooperative-u
runs.answer: Affected French chains: Intermarché (about 150 stores, owner Les Mousquetaires, plus its Netto banner), Coopérative U (including Super U), Carrefour Market, Monoprix and E.Leclerc (France's largest chain; Auchan was contacted but didn't comment). French outlets reported roughly 250–350 stores hit. Attackers hijacked internet-exposed Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA refrigeration controllers running older control software and triggered their built-in automatic defrosting to push fridge temperatures up to 50C for about six hours, spoiling fresh/frozen food and reportedly causing fires; CISA had warned in 2025 of two Danfoss flaws (CVE-2025-41450 auth bypass, CVE-2025-41451 command injection), and researchers found ~1,590 Danfoss systems exposed in France. Intermarché said fresh/frozen display units were out of service and it pulled products "as quickly as possible"; Les Mousquetaires said it threw all food away to avoid health risks; Coopérative U's CEO Dominique Schelcher confirmed the attack, called it "extremely serious and unprecedented... unacceptable," and said an investigation would be conducted. The Paris prosecutor opened an investigation and ANSSI was tasked to probe it. On store opening

runs.title: Selma Blair: what happened on that flight?
runs.prompt: Actress Selma Blair was reportedly arrested after an incident on a Delta flight on Sunday 12 October 2026. A reader would ask: what is she accused of, and what have authorities said? Using only plain page fetches, find a factual, non-paywalled account of what happened on the flight and what charges or investigation she now faces. Start with the CBS News report and the Fox 10 report: https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/selma-blair-arrested-incident-on-board-flight-from-lax-to-jfk/ and https://www.fox10tv.com/2026/10/12/actress-selma-blair-arrested-accused-attacking-flight-staff/
runs.answer: On Sunday night (Oct. 11-12, 2026), Selma Blair, 54, was arrested after an incident aboard Delta Air Lines Flight 938 from Los Angeles (LAX) to New York's JFK. According to police and law-enforcement sources, she allegedly tried to open a plane door mid-flight, hit one flight attendant and bit another; two flight attendants were injured (one bitten, one with a laceration) and one was hospitalized, and the crew restrained her. Port Authority Police and the FBI were called to the gate around 11 p.m.; Blair was taken to Jamaica Hospital for evaluation, where she allegedly kicked a PAPD officer in the ambulance and assaulted a nurse. The FBI said it is investigating a "potential assault" onboard, and a law-enforcement source told CBS the FBI is charging her with two counts of assault (Fox 10 noted charges were not yet clear at its publication). Blair's attorney said she "experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct," received immediate medical attention and is in stable condition; she remains in custody and her service dog is with her attorney. Delta said it has "zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior."
